newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says G7 message sufficient sign to markets.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says G7 message sufficient sign to markets.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday the Group of Seven nations' statements on the currencies were designed as a clear signal to the markets and that they should be understood as such.

"There are three sentences. They are clear," Waigel said at a news conference after the one-day meeting concluded. "They show a signal, and I think they are sufficient for a reaction and as a signal for the markets."
The seven nations, the United States, Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain, said currencies should reflect fundamentals and that excessive volatitily was bad.
Waigel, however, said the agreement was not comparable to either the Plaza or Louvre Accords, put together in the mid 1980s, to curb the dollar's rise.
